cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Terms and Conditions
cards.instruction: Treat every offer, favor, feeling, and apology as a negotiation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I'll accept your apology for missing my birthday if I get first choice of Christmas dates.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum already expects me Christmas Day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Boxing Day, then. In exchange, I'll tell her I'm no longer hurt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather you actually stopped being hurt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay through New Year and I'll mean it. I'll even stop mentioning the birthday to Mum.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 controls apology acceptance and A3 delays questions, but A5 stays an ordinary negotiated condition rather than a distinct approval ruling.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 Christmas duty causes A3 Boxing Day offer; B4 real-feeling request causes A5 longer-stay terms, with an irrelevant A3 preface.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects Mum expectations and B4 asks for genuine repair, credibly resisting only performative forgiveness.

heightening.evidence: B4 sincerity demand causes A5 to price actual feeling rather than merely a report to Mum.

specificity.evidence: A1 missed birthday and Christmas dates establish family obligations and hurt clearly.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 extended stay for sincere forgiveness follows B4 precise request; the added status phrase is cumbersome.
